One lesson per level, taught by 'teacher' (dingo|wendy|kai). lines[]: character = who speaks (talk animation + caption), text = caption ({name} allowed), voice = mp3 path under assets/voice/ (empty = text only). Replace text/voice files freely; no code changes needed. Source: cooking-game/voices/script_kokoro/recap/recap_lines.json + docs/recap_teaching.md.

lessons.callout: Steps in order = a sequence of decisions

lines.text: Remember our very first soup? Onions, pot, cook, plate, serve!
In AI words, the cook is the agent. The kitchen is the environment.
Each moment in the kitchen is a state. Each move you pick is an action.
And the right order of actions makes the soup!

lessons.callout: You learn what you get rewarded for
terms: stars only for onions → zero soup
small stars for each helpful step → faster

lines.text: Level one was all about rewards! A reward is like a gold star.
When I only got stars for onions, I just piled up onions. Zero soup!
So reward design matters. You learn what you get rewarded for.
Good rewards, like small stars for each helpful step, taught us much faster.

lessons.callout: Try a lot first, then use what works

lines.text: Level two was about exploring. It means trying new things.
With zero curiosity, we kept bumping into walls. No soup at all.
So at first, try a lot. Later, use what works best. That's exploitation.
Trying, and trying again, is how we learned. That's training!

terms: value = a guess of how good an action is
solid bubble = sure, dashed = not so sure

lines.text: Level three asked a big question: is the AI sure?
Each action has a value. That's a guess of how good it will be.
Solid bubbles meant sure. Dashed bubbles meant not so sure.
If our confidence is low, don't trust us too much. Think for yourself!

terms: team score = my score + Kai's score
fewer stars for me can mean a better team

lines.text: Level four was teamwork! You played me, and Kai cooked beside you.
Two agents working together is called multi-agent cooperation.
The team score is my score plus Kai's score, added up.
Sometimes you get fewer stars, but the team does better. That's okay.
Now you know how AI learns. Great job, little chefs!
